data.question: How many customers (people) placed more than one order, counting all orders regardless of status?

steps: Query the customers and orders tables, joining them on customer_id.
Group by customer_unique_id to count total orders per person without applying any status filter.
Filter for customers where the order count is greater than one and return the total number of such customers.

args.purpose: Count customers with more than one order regardless of order status
args.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_order_customers
FROM (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM customers c
    JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
    HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1
) sub;

args.purpose: Check total distinct customers and distribution of order counts
args.sql:
SELECT 
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS total_customers,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_count = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS one_order_customers,
    SUM(CASE WHEN order_count > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS multi_order_customers
FROM (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM customers c
    JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
) sub;
